allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.3 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves; white flower spikes.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its spike drawn flower by flower (spec rework L1c): its kind from its characters, by the rule at the flowering plants; about 60 flowers, by eye (floras say only that they are numerous), each a tuft of nine white stamens about 5 mm across drawn as a flower of nine thread-like petals. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): no perianth, a tuft of nine stamens (their length by hand: stamens 3 to 4 mm, the Flora of North America, as quoted in search results) round a one-carpelled pistil, from the characters of Berberidaceae and Achlys by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.flower.inflorescence.k.note: How PlantGen lays out an inflorescence, a choice of the model's (spec rework L1): the inflorescence characters set the cluster of any look a taxon draws as one (`"inflorescence": {}`), its kind, how many units it bears on each axis, its primary branches and how it holds itself. Sizes, stalks and spacing stay set by hand until programs size their organs from characters.

appearance.organs.flower.shape.carpels.note: How PlantGen draws a flower, a choice of the model's (spec rework P5): the flower characters set a flower card's perianth, its parts, how they differ by place, how far the corolla is joined into a tube, a floral cup, where the ovary sits, a resupinate flower's turn, its stamens, staminodes and carpels and its spurs. The rules also set these fields in a season's flower and bud looks that draw a flower, unless set there by hand.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.note: The leaf drawn as a palmately compound leaf of three leaflets (spec rework P4), set from its characters by the rules at the flowering plants; before, one round blade stood in for it. By eye from photographs: the side leaflets held out level, 190 degrees apart, each leaflet a fan widening from a narrow foot to a broad, flat, toothed edge. The card now holds a stub of the stalk, so the leaf is drawn 15 cm long where its blade was 11 cm.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.leaflets.note: How PlantGen draws a divided leaf, a choice of the model's (spec rework P4): the leaf characters set a compound card's pattern, its leaflets or pinnae, the leaflets on each pinna, and whether its segments run together. A pinnate leaf's count says how it ends (odd-pinnate odd, even-pinnate even), so a flora's range is drawn as the nearest count of the right kind.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a carpet-forming herb: each stalk holds a flat leaf of three broad, fan-shaped leaflets, with a slender spike of tiny white flowers above. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

generator.spreads.params.stem_height.note: What the herb program's stem height means: each year's stems reach it at maturity, give or take height_spread, their flowers included, so a mature herb stands about as tall as a flora's usual height for the plant, read as the range's middle unless it names a typical height.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
